_provisional: Authored in Rebel-Sim per FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §0. As of M3, this is checked against the real Rebel-ROM reference implementation (a sibling checkout, not in this repo) rather than invented from the spec docs alone: sysvar GROUP NAMES, ORDER, and OFFSETS below match src/sysvars.h and src/screenmodule.h exactly. One deliberate divergence: Rebel-ROM packs sysvar fields as byte/u16 C structs; Rebel-Sim stores every field as a full 4-byte cell for uniformity with the rest of this engine, so FIELD offsets within each group do NOT match Rebel-ROM byte-for-byte, only the group-level map does. Primitive token IDs and the DICT/RSTK/CHAR bank contents are Rebel-Sim-only (Rebel-ROM's Forth/Phase 11 doesn't exist yet) and have no real counterpart to reconcile against.
_dovarDodoesNote: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §7: two more reserved Code Field sentinel values, same tier as docolTokenId (checked once at the START of executeXT, never iterated over in the slot-processing loop the way primitive token IDs are). Negative so they're visually and numerically distinct from both DOCOL (0) and the positive 1..N primitive token space, and from -1 (inner.ts's own TOP_LEVEL_SENTINEL, a return-stack VALUE, not a code-field value, so no real collision risk either way). A third sentinel, doconTokenId (-3), existed through M41 for CONSTANT's dedicated dispatch — removed per spec/04-FORTH-CORE.md §4.1's recommended default (no target-independent reason to keep a fourth sentinel once CONSTANT is fully expressible as CREATE , DOES> @, system.fth).

primitives.note: formats the popped number in the current BASE and streams it (plus a trailing space) through screen.emit(), one character at a time

primitives.name: EMIT
primitives.note: pops a raw character code and streams it through screen.emit() (M3: a real CHAR-bank + framebuffer write, matching Rebel-ROM's CScreenModule::Emit — \r/\n are handled as control codes there, not glyphs)

primitives.name: CR
primitives.note: M3: screen.emit(10) — Rebel-ROM's Emit() special-cases '\n' as cursor-to-next-row rather than treating CR as a HAL call of its own

primitives.name: EXIT
primitives.note: pops the return stack into IP; only meaningful inside a compiled word body, special-cased by the inner interpreter (M2)

primitives.name: LIT
primitives.note: pushes the next parameter-field cell as a data literal and skips over it; only meaningful inside a compiled word body, special-cased by the inner interpreter (M2)

primitives.name: CHAR!
primitives.note: ( col row code -- ) M3: CScreenModule::WriteChar's 3-arg default-ink/paper overload — writes the CHAR bank cell and blits the glyph via the injected ScreenHal

primitives.name: CHAR@
primitives.note: ( col row -- code ) M3: CScreenModule::ReadChar — reads the CHAR bank directly, no framebuffer involved; out-of-range returns 32 (space), matching Rebel-ROM

primitives.name: CLS
primitives.note: ( -- ) M3: CScreenModule::Cls — fills the CHAR bank with spaces, clears the framebuffer to the current PAPER color, resets the cursor to 0,0

primitives.name: AT-XY
primitives.note: ( col row -- ) M3: CScreenModule::SetCursor — sets CURSOR-X/CURSOR-Y directly, no bounds-checking (matching Rebel-ROM; an out-of-range cursor self-corrects on the next EMIT via AdvanceCursor's wrap)

primitives.name: INK
primitives.note: ( color -- ) M3: sets the SCREEN group's default foreground color sysvar used by CHAR!/EMIT/. when no override is given. Rebel-Sim stores this as a raw 24-bit 0xRRGGBB truecolor value (Rebel-ROM's TColor is likewise a raw pixel value, not a palette index — direct/truecolor mode is its likely default per docs/SCREEN-MODULE.md §4)

primitives.name: PAPER
primitives.note: ( color -- ) M3: same as INK but for the background color

primitives.name: KEY?
primitives.note: ( -- flag ) M4: CKeyboardModule::ReadEvent peeked non-destructively — TRUE if the event queue is non-empty, matching FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md's hal_key_pressed? non-blocking-read requirement

primitives.name: KEY
primitives.note: ( -- char ) M7: blocks (FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §7a) — suspends the running session via inner.ts's generator-based step loop until the bound Channel (channel.ts, default KeyboardChannel) has a translated-char event, then pops and pushes it. M4's original throw-on-empty behavior is gone; KEY?/token 29 is unchanged (still a raw, unfiltered, non-blocking peek at the Keyboard queue).

primitives.name: ACCEPT
primitives.note: ( addr len -- len2 ) M7a: classic Forth line-input. Reads chars one at a time off the bound Channel (blocking, like KEY), echoing each via screen.emit() and storing into the arena at addr; Backspace (char 8) erases the last echoed char (wraps back across a screen row boundary if needed) without going below the start of this call's input; Enter (char 10) terminates without being stored. Fully special-cased in inner.ts's dispatch — never reaches primitives.ts's switch, since it needs many blocking points (one per character), not just one.
( addr -- x ) M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §4: cell fetch. addr must be cell-aligned — no defined behavior for misaligned reads, matching the cell model.
( x addr -- ) cell store, same alignment requirement.

primitives.name: C@
primitives.note: ( addr -- x ) byte fetch, zero-extended, no alignment requirement.

primitives.name: C!
primitives.note: ( x addr -- ) byte store (low 8 bits of x).
( n addr -- ) add n to the cell at addr. STANDARD-for-now per §3 (DUP @ ROT + SWAP ! once LOAD exists) but shipped as a primitive today, same reasoning as everything in §9.

primitives.name: >R
primitives.note: ( x -- ) ( R: -- x ) M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §5: move top of data stack to return stack. Unbalanced against R>/EXIT corrupts the return address — a real, documented footgun this spec doesn't guard against, not an oversight.

primitives.name: R>
primitives.note: ( -- x ) ( R: x -- ) move top of return stack to data stack.

primitives.name: R@
primitives.note: ( -- x ) ( R: x -- x ) copy top of return stack without removing it.

primitives.name: BRANCH
primitives.note: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §6: unconditional jump — reads the next cell as a target ip value and jumps there. Only meaningful inside a compiled word body; special-cased by the inner interpreter exactly like LIT/EXIT (M2), not a primitives.ts case. Never dictionary-called directly.

primitives.name: 0BRANCH
primitives.note: conditional jump — pops a flag; FALSE behaves like BRANCH, TRUE skips the target cell and continues. Same inner-interpreter special-casing as BRANCH.

primitives.name: (DO)
primitives.note: Runtime helper LOOP-family words compile calls to — not meant to be typed directly (parenthesized, classic-Forth convention for 'internal'). Pops limit then index off the data stack, pushes them onto RSTK above the current return address (docs §5's >R/R> warning applies to this pairing too).

primitives.name: (LOOP)
primitives.note: Runtime helper: increments RSTK's loop index by 1, compares to the limit; pushes FALSE (continue — LOOP's compiled 0BRANCH will jump back) or TRUE (done) onto the data stack; on done, also drops the loop-control cells off RSTK.

primitives.name: (+LOOP)
primitives.note: Runtime helper: as (LOOP), but pops the increment off the data stack instead of using 1.

primitives.name: (DOES>)
primitives.note: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §7: what DOES> compiles a call to. Only meaningful inside a compiled word body; special-cased by the inner interpreter (needs the live ip register and performs an EXIT-like return-stack unwind), never dictionary-called directly. At runtime: rewrites LATEST's own Code Field to dodoesTokenId, stores the current ip (which — since this dispatch already advanced past its own slot — is exactly the address of the code following DOES> in the *defining* word) into LATEST's leading parameter-field cell (the does-pointer DODOES reads), then ip = rstack.pop() (unwinds back to whatever called the defining word).

primitives.name: HERE
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) current dictionary-growth pointer — already tracked internally since M2, just not callable from Forth until now.

primitives.name: LATEST
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) address of the most recently defined dictionary entry — same situation as HERE. Needed by any dictionary-walking word (WORDS, §12).
( x -- ) compiles x as the next cell at HERE, advancing HERE — the same primitive compileCell() (dictionary.ts) already does internally, now exposed to Forth source.

primitives.name: ALLOT
primitives.note: ( n -- ) advances HERE by n bytes without writing anything — reserves raw space.

primitives.name: CREATE
primitives.note: ( "name" -- ) consumes the next input word as the name (same mechanism as VARIABLE), creates a dovarTokenId-coded entry and compiles one leading cell (initialized to 0) — the does-pointer slot DODOES reads *if* DOES> is later applied to this word; permanently unused otherwise, the one fixed cost of not knowing in advance whether DOES> is coming. Executing the new word (before any DOES>) pushes the address *past* that reserved cell — wherever HERE happens to be right after CREATE returns, exactly where a following `,`/ALLOT starts writing.

primitives.name: DOES>
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: compiles a single call to (DOES>). Everything else about the CREATE...DOES> mechanism lives in (DOES>)'s own runtime behavior and dodoesTokenId's dispatch, not here.

primitives.name: (SLIT)
primitives.note: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §8: string-literal runtime helper, generalizing LIT's inline-literal mechanism (FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §5) to a byte run instead of one cell. Only meaningful inside a compiled word body; special-cased by the inner interpreter: reads the next cell as a byte length, pushes (ip, length) as the string's addr/len, then advances ip past the string bytes rounded up to the next cell boundary (alignCell) — never dictionary-called directly.

primitives.name: S"
primitives.note: ( "string" -- addr len ) IMMEDIATE, dual-mode (DEVELOPING.md §7, M16): while compiling, compiles (SLIT) + the string's byte length + the raw string bytes inline, same as before; while interpreting, copies the text into the PAD bank and pushes its addr/len directly — real interpret-time behavior, not a throw. Multi-word strings work in both modes (DEVELOPING.md §2.4). PAD text longer than PAD's size throws rather than corrupting adjacent arena memory.

primitives.name: TYPE
primitives.note: ( addr len -- ) prints len characters starting at addr through screen.emit(), looped.

( "string" -- ) IMMEDIATE, dual-mode (DEVELOPING.md §7, M16): while compiling, sugar for S" ... TYPE, unchanged; while interpreting, emits the text directly through screen.emit() with no PAD involvement (nothing needs to persist past the print).

primitives.name: 2DUP
primitives.note: ( a b -- a b a b ) M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §9: STANDARD-for-now, shipped as a primitive since there's no loader yet (§3).

primitives.name: -ROT
primitives.note: ( a b c -- c a b )

primitives.name: TUCK
primitives.note: ( a b -- b a b )

primitives.name: NIP
primitives.note: ( a b -- b )

primitives.name: ?DUP
primitives.note: ( x -- x x ) if x is nonzero, ( x -- x ) otherwise.

primitives.name: DEPTH
primitives.note: ( -- n ) current data stack depth.

primitives.name: /MOD
primitives.note: ( a b -- rem quot )

primitives.name: MIN
primitives.note: ( a b -- min )

primitives.name: MAX
primitives.note: ( a b -- max )
( n -- n/2 ) arithmetic shift right by 1.
( a b -- flag ) M1 shipped = but not its negation.
( n -- flag )
( n -- flag )

primitives.name: U<
primitives.note: ( a b -- flag ) unsigned comparison.

DEVELOPING.md §2: comment. ( -- ) IMMEDIATE, not compile-only — consumes input up to the matching ')' and discards it, compiling or not, classic Forth style. M11 originally retained it as compiled (SLIT)+2DROP inline data so SEE could echo it back; reverted M44 once SEE proved unable to tell it apart from a genuine discarded string.

DEVELOPING.md §6 (system vocabulary loading): tick. ( -- xt ) Not IMMEDIATE — runs at execution time like CREATE, so a Forth-defined word that compiles a call to ' (e.g. `: SEE ' ... ;`) correctly consumes its *caller's* next input word when it executes, the same shared-cursor mechanism CREATE already relies on. Parses the next input word, looks it up, errors (`? unrecognized word`) if not found, else pushes its cfa. Added specifically because there was previously no way for Forth-level source to resolve a name to an xt at runtime — a real, necessary primitive addition, not a SEE-specific hack.

primitives.name: LATEST-ADDR
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md §8 (VOCABULARY/USE): ( -- addr ) pushes the raw arena address of the LATEST sysvar cell itself (not its current value — LATEST already does that), so ordinary @/! can read and write it directly. Real Forth systems usually expose HERE/LATEST/STATE/BASE as ordinary variables rather than read-only accessors; this fixes that gap for LATEST specifically, the one VOCABULARY/USE need, rather than a blanket change.

primitives.name: EXECUTE
primitives.note: ( xt -- ) pops a code-field address and runs it exactly as if it had been called directly — DOCOL threading, DOVAR/DOCON/DODOES dispatch, breakpoints, and a blocking word (KEY/ACCEPT) inside it all behave identically to a normal call. Special-cased in inner.ts's dispatch(), never reaches primitives.ts's switch, because it needs to recurse into executeXT() itself (generator-level access a plain stack-effect primitive doesn't have), the same reason ACCEPT is handled there instead of here.

primitives.name: PAD
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) DEVELOPING.md §7, M16: pushes the base address of the PAD bank — the fixed, overwritten-on-next-use scratch region S" now copies interpreted-mode string text into. A free addition mirroring the HERE/LATEST precedent: PAD already needed to exist as a bank for S" to work, so exposing its address to Forth source costs nothing extra.

primitives.name: ABORT
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §9, M17: empties the data stack and throws a plain Error('ABORT'), surfacing via the same uncaught-error path every other error already uses (prints '? ABORT' at the top-level REPL). Deliberately NOT built on THROW/CATCH — that fuller exception model was scoped and then explicitly tabled ('probably not, unless a real need shows up'); this is the classic-Forth-useful subset of it that doesn't need any of that machinery.

primitives.name: BANK@
primitives.note: ( "name" -- addr ) IMMEDIATE, dual-mode (M53): parses the next input token (same nextInputToken() mechanism '/CREATE/VARIABLE/CONSTANT/S"/VOCABULARY/USE already use), uppercases it, looks up the bank with that exact name, or throws '? unknown bank: <NAME>' on no match. Resolves by name, not tag (Oliver + M50, found while adding BANK-SIZE): name is the real, uniqueness-backed identity (banks.ts) — tag is expected to repeat once multiple banks share one (project DATA assets, a future second BLKS-tagged bank, ...), so a tag-keyed lookup could only ever reach whichever same-tagged bank happened to be created first, silently hiding every other one. Every boot bank has an explicit name now (repl.ts) — the fixed system banks (SYSV/DSTK/RSTK/DICT/CHAR/KMAP/WORK) all have name == tag, so 'BANK@ SYSV'-style lookups are unaffected; only banks that share a tag (BLKS -> EDITOR) need their real name instead of the tag. addr only, matching the SOMETHING@ convention (fetch one value) — size is BANK-SIZE (144)'s job. Reaches shared and per-arena banks identically, no special-casing — multi-arena isolation is a confirmed non-goal (DEVELOPING.md §10), not something BANK@ needs to enforce. Combined with each sysvar group's known baseOffset (this file's sysvarGroups) and a field's own offset, 'BANK@ SYSV <offset> + @' reaches any sysvar from pure Forth source without a separate named-lookup primitive. Made IMMEDIATE + dual-mode at M53 (Oliver, found trying '`: TESTING BANK@ CHAR ;`'): previously a plain non-immediate BANK@ compiled a call to itself, leaving the compiler's own outer loop to try (and fail) to look up the following name token as an ordinary word, long before the name was ever meant to be consumed at runtime. Now the name is resolved right away, at compile time, and the result is compiled in as a LIT literal (S"/."'s STATE-dispatch pattern, case 68/70 — but LIT, not (SLIT), since a bank address is one cell, not a byte run); interpreted-mode behavior (push the address directly) is unchanged. This bakes the bank's address in at define-time — correct for the fixed system banks and any bank already created and stable when the defining word is compiled, but stale if that bank is later dropped and recreated at a new address.

primitives.name: CREATE-BANK
primitives.note: ( size "tag" -- addr ) DEVELOPING.md §13/§23, M21/M30: pops size, parses the next input token as the tag, uppercases it, and calls ctx.banks.createBank(tag, size) — the same BankTable.createBank() any host-side creation goes through (M30, PLAN.md: routes through the real size-class-rounding path instead of M21's original direct mmap.allocate() bypass). No name argument given, so the bank gets an auto-generated serial name from MMAP's own header counter, not the tag — a bank made via CREATE-BANK MYBANK is reachable later by that real serial name or by the address already returned, but not via BANK@ MYBANK, since MYBANK became its tag, not its name (M50: BANK@ resolves by name). Visible to BankTable.getAllBanks()/findBank() and everything built on them (storage.ts, the app's read_banks WebMCP tool, the inspector panel) since M30 — unlike the original M21 design, nothing bypasses BankTable anymore.

primitives.name: XOR
primitives.note: ( a b -- a^b ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: same shape as AND(15)/OR(16) — a real bitwise op the M8 batch never shipped.

primitives.name: .S
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: non-destructive stack print, bottom-to-top, current BASE — reuses .'s (18) own digit-formatting loop applied to every cell (stack.ts's toArray() is top-to-bottom, reversed here to print deepest-first, matching classic Forth .S).

primitives.name: 2SWAP
primitives.note: ( a b c d -- c d a b ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: swaps the top two cell-pairs.

primitives.name: 2OVER
primitives.note: ( a b c d -- a b c d a b ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: copies the second-from-top pair to the top, generalizing OVER(4) the way 2DUP/2DROP(71/72) generalized DUP/DROP.

primitives.name: CELLS
primitives.note: ( n -- n*4 ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: n * CELL_SIZE.

primitives.name: CELL+
primitives.note: ( addr -- addr+4 ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: addr + CELL_SIZE.

primitives.name: FILL
primitives.note: ( addr len char -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: classic ANS signature — fills len bytes starting at addr with char's low 8 bits.

primitives.name: CMOVE
primitives.note: ( addr1 addr2 len -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: copies len bytes addr1->addr2, low-to-high. Like real Forth's CMOVE (not CMOVE>), an overlapping range where addr2 falls inside [addr1, addr1+len) corrupts data — a documented footgun, not a bug, same precedent as the >R/R>(37) imbalance note.

primitives.name: BL
primitives.note: ( -- 32 ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: pushes the ASCII space code — named as a candidate in CORE-VOCABULARY.md §12 itself.

primitives.name: SPACE
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: BL EMIT as one word.

primitives.name: WITHIN
primitives.note: ( n lo hi -- flag ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: TRUE if lo <= n < hi. Deliberately plain signed, non-wraparound semantics, not full ANS WITHIN's modular-arithmetic definition — U<(92) already covers the one place unsigned comparison was actually needed, and no current caller needs wraparound ranges.

primitives.name: PICK
primitives.note: ( xu ... x1 x0 u -- xu ... x1 x0 xu ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: generalizes OVER (1 PICK = OVER, 0 PICK = DUP) to arbitrary depth.

primitives.name: ROLL
primitives.note: ( xu ... x1 x0 u -- xu-1 ... x1 x0 xu ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: generalizes ROT (2 ROLL = ROT) — pops u, then the item u cells down, shifting everything above it down by one and pushing the rolled item on top.

primitives.name: BASE
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) DEVELOPING.md §16, M24: pushes the arena address of the FORTH.BASE sysvar cell — a real Forth variable, not a read-only value word like HERE/LATEST. Read with BASE @, write with n BASE !. Same fieldOffset() reuse pattern LATEST-ADDR(95) established for VOCABULARY/USE.

primitives.name: HEX
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §16, M24: sets BASE to 16.

primitives.name: DECIMAL
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §16, M24: sets BASE to 10.

primitives.name: CURSEN
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §17, M25: turns the visible text cursor on — sets SCREEN.CURSOR-VISIBLE TRUE and immediately redraws the current cursor cell inverted (ink/paper swapped). Screen-level, not HAL: hooks into Screen.setCursor() so AT-XY/EMIT's auto-advance/CR/LF all move the visible cursor correctly for free.

primitives.name: CURSDIS
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §17, M25: turns the visible text cursor off — sets SCREEN.CURSOR-VISIBLE FALSE and redraws the current cell normally.

primitives.name: SP0
primitives.note: ( -- a-addr ) DEVELOPING.md §21, M28: pushes FORTH.SP0, the constant address the data stack pointer equals when empty.

primitives.name: SP@
primitives.note: ( -- a-addr ) DEVELOPING.md §21, M28: pushes FORTH.SP, the live data stack pointer (the address of the current top-of-stack cell, or SP0 if empty).

primitives.name: SP!
primitives.note: ( a-addr -- ) DEVELOPING.md §21, M28: pops an address, writes it into FORTH.SP — the standard SP0 SP! stack-reset idiom. No bounds validation — an address outside DSTK isn't caught until the next push/pop/peek.

primitives.name: RP0
primitives.note: ( -- a-addr ) DEVELOPING.md §21, M28: same as SP0, for the return stack (FORTH.RP0).

primitives.name: RP@
primitives.note: ( -- a-addr ) DEVELOPING.md §21, M28: same as SP@, for the return stack (FORTH.RP).

primitives.name: RP!
primitives.note: ( a-addr -- ) DEVELOPING.md §21, M28: same as SP!, for the return stack. Real risk, not hypothetical: the return stack holds live return addresses for every word currently executing — a wrong RP! mid-execution corrupts the call chain, same 'authentic risk, no host-side validation' stance as MMAP's raw writes.

primitives.name: HERE-ADDR
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md §8.6, FORGET: ( -- addr ) pushes the raw arena address of the HERE sysvar cell itself (not its current value — HERE already does that), so ordinary @/! can read and write it directly, the same pattern LATEST-ADDR (95) established for VOCABULARY/USE. Unblocks FORGET as pure Forth source: reclaiming a forgotten word's DICT space needs to roll HERE back to that word's own address, not just relink LATEST past it.

primitives.name: PROJECT
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md's storage section, M33: ( "name" -- ) sets the current project name sysvar. Was outer-loop-only special syntax in repl.ts (like `:`/`;`) back when SAVE/RESTORE needed to suspend the interpreter around a Promise-based OPFS call; now that StorageHal is synchronous (local-storage-storage-hal.ts), this is an ordinary primitive, usable inside a colon-definition or via EXECUTE like any other word.

primitives.name: SAVE
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md's storage section, M33: ( -- ) writes every currently active bank (MMAP included, in MMAP slot order) as a project asset under the current PROJECT name; throws if none is set. Same demotion from outer-loop-only syntax to an ordinary primitive as PROJECT (126), now that storage is synchronous.

primitives.name: RESTORE
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md's storage section, M33: ( "name" -- ) loads a previously-saved project via Storage.openProject()'s MMAP-first two-phase restore, sets it as the current project, and repaints the screen (a restore overwrites CHAR bytes directly, bypassing the normal per-character write-through). Same demotion from outer-loop-only syntax to an ordinary primitive as PROJECT (126). M54: never reaches primitives.ts's switch any more -- inner.ts's dispatch() special-cases this token entirely, same tier as COLD (132)/ACCEPT/EXECUTE, because a resize-triggered restart (a BANK-RESIZE, 146, that was SAVEd) needs to yield a StepSignal instead of running in place. projectNeedsRestart()/restoreProject() (primitives.ts) hold the actual logic now; dispatch() picks between them after parsing the project name once.

primitives.name: BSAVE
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md's storage section, M33: ( "tag" -- ) saves just one already-existing bank (resolved by tag, same BankTable.requireBank() single-tag addressing BANK@ (99) uses) as a project asset under the current PROJECT name; throws if none is set. The single-bank counterpart to SAVE (127), added once storage stopped needing a suspend/resume mechanism to reach.

primitives.name: BLOAD
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md's storage section, M33: ( "tag" -- ) overwrites one already-existing bank's own memory in place from its previously-BSAVEd (129) asset under the current PROJECT name; throws if none was ever saved. Repaints the screen only when the loaded bank is CHAR, same reasoning as RESTORE (128). The single-bank counterpart to RESTORE.

primitives.name: WARM
primitives.note: Soft reset ( -- ): clears the data and return stacks, but leaves DICT and MMAP untouched — the running dictionary and bank layout survive. Handled entirely in primitives.ts; the engine performs the reset in place, no host involvement needed.

primitives.name: COLD
primitives.note: Full reset ( -- ): equivalent to a fresh boot, DICT and MMAP included. Machine's memory-holding fields are readonly and built once in the constructor, so this can't be done in place — dispatch() (inner.ts) special-cases this token before it ever reaches executePrimitive, yielding a 'cold' StepSignal instead of executing anything. The host (packages/app's tick()) sees Machine.step() return the 'cold' StepStatus and reconstructs the Machine from scratch. Never reaches primitives.ts's switch, same shape as ACCEPT/EXECUTE.

primitives.name: REDRAW
primitives.note: ( -- ) Repaints the whole framebuffer from CHAR bank content, cell by cell — Screen.redrawAll(), the same mechanism RESTORE (128) and BLOAD (130) already call internally after overwriting CHAR bytes directly. Exposes it as an ordinary word for the same reason those need it: writing CHAR directly (e.g. BANK@ CHAR ... C!) bypasses writeChar()'s per-character HAL write-through, so nothing else repaints the visible screen from a poke like that. Real cross-target precedent, not web-only: matches rebel-rom's CScreenModule::Redraw() (src/screenmodule.h/.cpp) bit for bit in purpose — 'repaints every cell from m_pCharBank's current contents' — used there by AttachArena() after repointing the shared screen at a different arena's CHAR bank.

primitives.name: WORD
primitives.note: ( char "<chars>ccc<char>" -- addr len ) spec/04-FORTH-CORE.md §6.13: skips leading char bytes from the shared input cursor, reads up to the next char or end of line, advances the cursor past what was read (consuming a trailing delimiter, if one was hit). Returns a view into the live TIB, not a copy — INTERPRET (system.fth) is the main consumer, walking a line with BL as the delimiter, but any char works.

primitives.name: STATE
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) direct address of the FORTH.STATE sysvar cell — same pattern as BASE/HERE-ADDR/LATEST-ADDR. The foundation [ / ] / INTERPRET (system.fth, §6.13) read and write directly.

( "name" -- ) spec/04-FORTH-CORE.md §5.2: begins a definition — reads the next raw token as the new word's name, writes its dictionary header immediately (HIDDEN, so RECURSE can find it another way), switches to compiling. Not IMMEDIATE; dispatched like any other word found while interpreting — no longer special-cased by spelling (M43).

( -- ) IMMEDIATE — §5.2: ends a definition. Compiles a trailing EXIT, clears HIDDEN, switches to interpreting. MUST carry IMMEDIATE (INTERPRET's compiling-mode dispatch, not spelling, is what makes it run instead of compile) and self-checks STATE, since nothing external gates that once dispatch is uniform (M43).

primitives.name: IMMEDIATE
primitives.note: ( -- ) §5.2: sets the IMMEDIATE flag on LATEST. Not itself IMMEDIATE — always typed and executed directly at the prompt, never compiled into another definition. No longer special-cased by spelling (M43).

primitives.name: COMPILE-ONLY
primitives.note: ( -- ) sets the COMPILE-ONLY flag on LATEST — the same bootstrap-marking mechanism IMMEDIATE (138) is, added in M42 as a special-cased keyword (nothing else could reach the flag yet) and promoted to an ordinary primitive here (M43) for the same reason :/;/IMMEDIATE are: never special-cased by spelling. Not part of spec/04-FORTH-CORE.md's own vocabulary, which predates M42.

primitives.name: (BLOCK-READ)
primitives.note: ( addr n -- ) FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §7's hal_block_read(n, addr): copies block n's 1024 bytes from the resident BLKS bank into RAM at addr. Paren-named like (DO)/(LOOP)/(+LOOP) (53-55) — an internal primitive Forth-level BLOCK/BUFFER (not yet built, system.fth) will call, not something meant to be typed directly. Throws if n is outside BLKS's fixed 16-block capacity (bounds-checked here, not left to DataView) — same 'unknown bank'-style loud failure BANK@ (99) uses.

primitives.name: (BLOCK-WRITE)
primitives.note: ( addr n -- ) FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §7's hal_block_write(n, addr): copies 1024 bytes from RAM at addr into block n of the resident BLKS bank. The write-back half of (BLOCK-READ) (140) — same bounds check, same paren-naming convention, same future caller (BLOCK/BUFFER/UPDATE/FLUSH). Does not itself persist to disk — SAVE/BSAVE (already built, M5/M33) do that for the whole BLKS bank at project save time, same as any other bank.

primitives.name: (SET-INPUT)
primitives.note: ( addr len -- ) FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §7's Screen Editor follow-up: repoints the shared input cursor (repl.ts's inputPos/inputEnd) at an arbitrary region instead of the TIB. LOAD (system.fth) is the one caller — feeds a BLOCK-resident screen line through the exact same WORD/FIND/NUMBER/INTERPRET machinery an ordinary typed REPL line uses, one line at a time. Paren-named like (BLOCK-READ)/(BLOCK-WRITE) (140/141): internal plumbing, not meant to be typed directly. No bounds validation, same trust-the-caller precedent WORD itself already has.

primitives.name: VERSION
primitives.note: ( -- ) prints "Rebel Forth vMAJOR.MILESTONE.BUILD" plus a trailing CR — the startup banner packages/app's boot sequence (app.ts) prints once, right after system.fth loads and before the REPL's first prompt. MAJOR/MILESTONE (version.ts) are hand-bumped alongside PLAN.md's own M-numbered milestone log; BUILD (build-info.ts) is regenerated fresh on every build (packages/engine's own pretest/prebuild hooks), never hand-edited, never committed — the cheapest way to tell a stale cached page apart from a freshly built one. Deliberately native, not a SYSV field: build identity is static per-build metadata, not live interpreter state like BASE/HERE, and SYSV groups are meant to be generated from the same cross-target layout as Rebel-ROM's real sysvars.h, which has no version-field counterpart to stay in sync with.

primitives.name: BANK-SIZE
primitives.note: ( "name" -- size ) IMMEDIATE, dual-mode: reads a bank's actual size (already rounded up to its size class at creation, banks.ts's createBank) — the read-only counterpart BANK@ (99) never had. Same parsed-word name lookup as BANK@ (M50: switched from tag), same "unknown bank" error. First real consumer: a future capacity display (e.g. DICT used/free). Deliberately read-only — spec/02-MEMORY-MODEL.md §7 explicitly defers any richer resize/reallocate model ("do not design ahead of these"): banks are handed out by a pure bump allocator with no compaction or relocation ever, so resizing anything but the most-recently-created bank would mean either relocating it (rewriting every absolute address anyone holds into it — infeasible for DICT once anything's compiled) or leaking the freed space (no freelist exists). Made IMMEDIATE + dual-mode (Oliver, same bug class BANK@ hit at M53): a plain non-immediate BANK-SIZE compiled a call to itself, leaving the compiler's own outer loop to try (and fail) to look up the following name token as an ordinary word (`: FOO BANK-SIZE SYSV ;` failed with "unrecognized word: SYSV"). Now the name is resolved at compile time and the result compiled in as a LIT literal, same as BANK@; interpreted-mode behavior (push the size directly) is unchanged. Bakes the bank's size in at define-time, so it goes stale the same way BANK@'s baked-in address does if that bank is later dropped and recreated at a different size.

primitives.name: PROJECTS
primitives.note: ( -- ) prints every project name currently under /PROJECTS/ (space separated) — storage.ts's Storage.listProjects(), a thin StorageHal.listDirs() wrapper. M51, requested by Oliver alongside BANKS (system.fth): same dev-ergonomics motivation, 'what actually exists right now,' but for the storage layer instead of the bank table. An ordinary sync primitive, same precedent as PROJECT/SAVE/RESTORE (126-128, M33's synchronous StorageHal migration) — genuinely usable inside a colon-definition or via EXECUTE, unlike the raw-token-consuming primitives (BANK@, PROJECT itself) whose argument is a *live* input token consumed at the moment they run: PROJECTS takes no argument at all, so that distinction doesn't apply to it.

primitives.name: BANK-RESIZE
primitives.note: ( new-size "name" -- ) M54, Oliver's idea: overwrites the named bank's own size field in MMAP (mmap.ts's setSlotSize(), reached via banks.ts's resizeBank()) with `new-size` rounded up to a size class, same rounding CREATE-BANK (100) applies. No bytes move, no other bank's base/size changes -- deliberately inert for the CURRENTLY RUNNING Machine: every consumer holding this bank's descriptor (DataStack, dictionary.ts's HERE-overflow check, Screen, Keyboard, ...) captured an immutable snapshot at construction time, and a bigger claimed region would physically overlap whichever bank sits right after it in memory today, since nothing shifts. Becomes real only across a save/restart cycle: SAVE (127) persists this MMAP edit, and a subsequent RESTORE (128) that finds a saved size differing from what's live now triggers a fresh Machine construction instead of an in-place restore (Inner's 'restart-project' StepSignal, mirroring COLD's own 'throw this one away, build a fresh one' shape) -- repl.ts's bootProject option re-derives every bank's base from these (possibly-edited) sizes via the normal bump allocator, the only point a resize can safely relocate whatever comes after it. DSTK/RSTK are unconditionally reset to empty across that restart (their live SP/RP sysvar cells are absolute addresses that a relayout can silently invalidate) -- data/return stack contents were never expected to survive it, same as WARM already resets both on a soft reset. MMAP itself can never be resized (banks.ts throws) -- its size is a fixed, asserted cross-target layout constant, not bump-allocated capacity. Not IMMEDIATE -- an action, not something a colon-definition needs to bake an address into (unlike BANK@, 99). Revisits spec/02-MEMORY-MODEL.md §7's prior 'do not design ahead of these' deferral now that a concrete, safe (restart-triggered, not in-place) mechanism exists; BANK-SIZE (144) stays read-only, this is the write path.

primitives.name: TERMINAL
primitives.note: ( -- ) M64/M65: connects this session to a target board over that target's own transport, handing over screen/keyboard to it -- a genuinely portable HAL-level word from the start (REMOTE-TERMINAL.md), not a Rebel-Sim-only convenience: this repo's own implementation (remote-terminal-protocol.ts/remote-board.ts/remote-terminal.ts) connects to an in-process simulated board, reachable with zero real hardware, while other targets are expected to implement it via their own real transport (serial/USB/TCP) to an actual attached board. Same 'can't happen in place, host must act' shape as COLD/RESTORE (132/128): inner.ts's dispatch() special-cases this token before executePrimitive ever runs and yields a dedicated 'terminal' StepSignal, carrying no payload (unlike RESTORE's project name, nothing else is needed) -- the host (packages/app's app.ts) does the actual connecting. Not IMMEDIATE -- an ordinary runtime action.

primitives.name: PLOT
primitives.note: ( x y -- ) M68: the one primitive the whole GRAPHICS vocabulary (system.fth) is built on -- sets one raw framebuffer pixel to the current INK sysvar (Screen.plot(), spec/01-HAL.md §3.4's hal_draw_pixel), the same implicit-color convention EMIT/CHAR! already use rather than taking color as a stack argument. Pixel space (SCREEN-WIDTH/SCREEN-HEIGHT), not character-cell space -- out-of-range x/y silently no-op, same convention as CHAR!. INK is resolved through the active palette exactly like writeChar's ink/paper before it ever reaches the HAL (spec/01-HAL.md §3.6) -- required, not optional, since M62 boots with the default palette already active, so the raw INK sysvar is the index 4, not literal green: skipping resolution would make a default-configuration PLOT draw near-black pixels. This does not give hal.drawPixel itself any palette awareness -- the HAL still only ever receives an already-resolved literal 0xRRGGBB value, never an index. Never touches CHAR/ATTR either. Every other GRAPHICS word (LINE/RECT/CIRCLE/...) is pure Forth built on this one call, per CLAUDE.md's 'primitives only if absolutely necessary' rule -- nothing else in this engine can reach a raw pixel.

primitives.name: POINT
primitives.note: ( x y -- color ) M68: the read-side counterpart of PLOT (148), completing the classic PLOT/POINT pairing -- reads one raw framebuffer pixel back (Screen.point(), spec/01-HAL.md §3.4's new hal_read_pixel). Out-of-range x/y return -1, a sentinel no legitimate 0xRRGGBB color can produce (0 is a real color, black -- reusing it would make 'nothing there' indistinguishable from 'black was plotted there'). Pixel readback is OPTIONAL at the cross-target HAL contract level (spec/01-HAL.md §3.4): a target with no readback path may implement hal_read_pixel as an always -1 stub rather than omitting POINT entirely, keeping the word itself portable even where the underlying capability isn't.

bankTags.DICT: dictionary / user program space, per-arena (in use since M2)
bankTags.RSTK: return stack, per-arena (in use since M2)
bankTags.CHAR: character-code grid, per-arena, 1 byte per cell, write-through into the framebuffer via ScreenHal (in use since M3, matches Rebel-ROM's CHAR bank exactly — docs/SCREEN-MODULE.md §3)
bankTags.SCRN: pixel framebuffer — NOT an arena bank in Rebel-Sim (matches Rebel-ROM: externally-backed, outside the arena's own memory accounting, excluded from the portable-dump claim per FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §8). Rebel-Sim's analog is the host-supplied ScreenHal implementation drawing to a <canvas>, never arena-resident memory.
bankTags.KMAP: raw-usage-code -> character translation table, u8[2][256] (unshifted/shifted planes), in use since M4 (docs/KEYBOARD.md §6). CLAUDE.md lists KMAP as shared/singular rather than per-arena like SCRN — Rebel-Sim only has one arena today (no multi-arena isolation yet), so it's allocated inside that arena like CHAR; the shared/singular distinction becomes visible once multi-arena support lands.
bankTags.FONT: glyph bitmap data (256 chars x 8 bytes, one row per byte, MSB = leftmost pixel), in use since M59 — loaded at boot from packages/app/public/rebel.FNT, address tracked in the FONT sysvar group's FONT-BASE field (spec/03-SYSVARS.md §8) rather than hardcoded, so a future font switch is just repointing that sysvar at a different FONT-tagged bank. Shared/singular like KMAP/SCRN, same reasoning (one physical rendering resource, not per-program state) and same one-arena-today caveat. Rebel-ROM's own font system stays compiled-in TFont structs with no Forth-addressable bank yet (docs/FONT-SYSTEM.md §6) — Rebel-Sim is ahead here, not matching an existing rebel-rom mechanism.
bankTags.PAL: indexed color palette, per-arena — up to 16 maps of 16 x 0xRRGGBB entries (64 bytes each, contiguous), map N at PAL-base + N*64 (spec/02-MEMORY-MODEL.md §4.6). Map slot 0 is normatively initialized to the default 16-color palette at boot. The active map's address is tracked by the SCREEN group's PALETTE-BASE field; 0 there means disabled (today's unmodified literal-RGB-only behavior).
bankTags.ATTR: per-cell ink/paper attribute byte (IIIIPPPP: high nibble = ink index, low nibble = paper index), per-arena, same size and addressing as CHAR (spec/02-MEMORY-MODEL.md §4.6). Write-through mirrors CHAR's while PALETTE-BASE is non-zero; inert (not written, not consulted) while it's 0.
bankTags.TIB: Terminal Input Buffer, per-arena, in use since M7a — the resident scratch region ACCEPT reads a REPL line into. Not a Rebel-ROM-derived tag (no shipped Rebel-ROM Phase 11 yet, same status as Rebel-Sim-only DATA/FORTH group precedent) and not a persistable project-asset bank — Storage never touches it.
bankTags.PAD: Scratch text region, per-arena, in use since M16 (DEVELOPING.md §7) — holds the text S" copies in while interpreting, so its addr/len can be pushed and used immediately (e.g. by TYPE) without needing dictionary space. Rebel-Sim-only, no Rebel-ROM Phase 11 precedent yet, same status as TIB. Deliberately not reused for anything else (no reentrancy/nesting support) — overwritten unconditionally on each S" call, a documented footgun matching real Forth's own PAD semantics. Not a persistable project-asset bank — Storage never touches it.
bankTags.BLKS: Generic 1024-byte-block-addressable storage, per-arena, fixed at 16 blocks (16 KiB, exactly one size class, no rounding waste) — FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §7's `hal_block_read`/`hal_block_write` porting note (renamed from `SCRS` 2026-08-18: the bank carries no screen/text assumption; classic Forth source-editing screens are its first consumer, not its definition). `(BLOCK-READ)`/`(BLOCK-WRITE)` (140/141) are the only primitives that touch it directly — plain memcpy against `BLKS-base + n*1024`, bounds-checked against the 16-block capacity. A persistable project-asset bank like any other (`.BLK` extension, storage.ts's TAG_TO_EXTENSION) — SAVE/RESTORE/BSAVE/BLOAD round-trip it whole; FLUSHing a dirty in-Forth buffer into it (once BLOCK/BUFFER/UPDATE/FLUSH exist in system.fth) is a separate, smaller act from persisting the whole bank to disk.

CORE.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_CORE_OFFSET (0x010). Real TCoreSysVars also has SCREEN-MODE/COLOR-DEPTH/PALETTE-BANK/KEYMAP/LAST-ERROR — not implemented in Rebel-Sim yet, added when something needs them, same reserved-slot precedent as everywhere else in this table.

CURSOR-X.note: text cursor column. M3: owned by Screen, not bounds-checked on write (matches Rebel-ROM's SetCursor)

SCREEN.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_SCREEN_OFFSET (0x040) and screenmodule.h's TScreenSysVars. COLOR-DEPTH/PALETTE-SIZE omitted — Rebel-Sim's canvas HAL is truecolor-only, no palette-indirection mode to track.

CHAR-CELL-W.note: current glyph cell width in pixels

CHAR-CELL-H.note: current glyph cell height in pixels

CHAR-COLS.note: character grid width = SCREEN-WIDTH / CHAR-CELL-W; the actual addressing stride into the CHAR bank (docs/SCREEN-MODULE.md §3.2), not recomputed on the fly

INK.note: default foreground color (0xRRGGBB) for character writes

PAPER.note: default background color (0xRRGGBB) for character writes

CURSOR-VISIBLE.note: DEVELOPING.md §17, M25: HAL boolean (TRUE=-1/FALSE=0), defaults FALSE. The reverse of this group's usual direction, same situation CORE.ARENA-SIZE (M19) was in: checked directly against rebel-rom/src/sysvars.h's real TScreenSysVars — it has no such field either, since no target renders a visible cursor yet — a genuine cross-target candidate proposed from the Rebel-Sim side, not Rebel-Sim-only.

PALETTE-BASE.note: Indexed color palette (spec/02-MEMORY-MODEL.md §4.6's PAL bank, spec/01-HAL.md §3.6): arena address of the active 16-entry 0xRRGGBB map, 0 = disabled (today's literal-RGB-only behavior, unchanged) — same address/0-disabled convention as FONT-BASE. Defaults FALSE (0) via the arena's own zero-init, same as CURSOR-VISIBLE — never explicitly set at boot.

KEYBOARD.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_KEYBOARD_OFFSET (0x080). M4: populated with MODIFIERS only — real TKeyboardSysVars also has nKeyboardCount (attached-device count), omitted here since browser DOM APIs have no USB-hotplug-style device enumeration to report; there's always implicitly 'some keyboard'.

MODIFIERS.note: live modifier bitmask (docs/KEYBOARD.md §2): bit0-3 = L Ctrl/Shift/Alt/GUI, bit4-7 = R Ctrl/Shift/Alt/GUI. Updated on every modifier press/release pseudo-event (0x80+bit convention).

FONT.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_FONT_OFFSET (0x0C0). M59: Rebel-Sim now has a real, arena-resident FONT bank (packages/app's rebel.FNT loaded at boot) — FONT-BASE tracks its address. Rebel-ROM's own Phase 6 font system stays compiled-in TFont structs with no Forth-addressable bank or runtime switching yet (docs/FONT-SYSTEM.md §6), so this is Rebel-Sim genuinely ahead here, not parity with an existing rebel-rom field.

FONT-BASE.note: arena address of the currently-active FONT-tagged bank (spec/03-SYSVARS.md §8). Set once at boot to the default FONT bank's base; repointing it at a different FONT-tagged bank is how a future font switch would work — no new mechanism needed for that.

STORAGE.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_STORAGE_OFFSET (0x140). MOUNTED(0)/LAST-ERROR(4)/DEVICE-SEEN(8) reserved by spec/01-HAL.md §6.6 but not yet implemented — PROJECT-NAME-0/1 appended after them, not renumbering.

PROJECT-NAME-0.note: chars 0-3 of the current project's 8-char name, NUL-padded ASCII packed 4-per-cell (same convention as bank tag/name fields, mmap.ts) — not Rebel-ROM's on-disk space-padded FAT-8.3 convention, a different layer. All-zero = unnamed project.

PROJECT-NAME-1.note: chars 4-7 of the current project's name — see PROJECT-NAME-0.

FORTH.note: Rebel-Sim-only group (Rebel-ROM's Phase 11/Forth doesn't exist yet) — appended after Rebel-ROM's real groups (STORAGE ends at 0x180) rather than colliding with them, same 64-byte-slot incremental-reservation pattern.

SP0.note: data stack base address (constant, = DSTK bank.base + bank.size) — written by DataStack's own constructor since DEVELOPING.md §21, M28

RP0.note: return stack base address (constant, = RSTK bank.base + bank.size) — same, for RSTK's DataStack instance

HERE.note: dictionary next-free pointer, grows up within DICT (in use since M2)

LATEST.note: most recently defined dictionary entry's address, 0 = empty dictionary (in use since M2)

SP.note: live data stack pointer (DEVELOPING.md §21, M28) — DataStack's own private sp field, relocated here so it's genuinely sysvar-backed, not an engine-side copy

RP.note: live return stack pointer (DEVELOPING.md §21, M28) — same relocation, for RSTK's DataStack instance
